ECE 6390 / Digital signals

Sampling & aliasing

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows why different continuous-time frequencies can produce identical sampled data.

Sampling observes a waveform only at t = n/fs. Adding an integer multiple of fs to a sinusoid's frequency adds integer multiples of 2π at those samples, leaving the sample sequence unchanged.

For a bandlimited baseband signal with highest frequency B, fs > 2B permits ideal reconstruction under the model's assumptions. An analog anti-alias filter must suppress unwanted energy before sampling.

Exactly at fs/2, a sinusoid's sampled appearance depends on phase and can be pathological. Aliasing is an ambiguity in the available samples, so filtering a recorded sequence cannot generally recover information already mixed together.

Example

A 900 Hz cosine sampled at 1,000 samples/s has the same real sample sequence as a 100 Hz cosine with the corresponding phase convention.
